core.title: Map every executable flow router guard path to exactly one user/system flow route or classify it as structural residual
core.given: A plan artifact containing a flow router with executable guard paths and the user/system flow routes projected from it
core.when: The plan reaches the CONFIRM phase (whether or not the flow router was changed)
core.then: Every executable guard path in the flow router maps to exactly one user/system flow route, unless it is explicitly classified as structural residual.
prefer: For each executable guard path, name the single user/system flow route that carries it, so the plan already satisfies the CONFIRM check.
When a guard path truly belongs to no route, mark it explicitly as structural residual instead of leaving it unmapped.
avoid: Leaving an executable guard path with no route and no explicit structural-residual classification.
Mapping a guard path that is not explicitly classified as structural residual to several routes.
Classifying routable guard paths as structural residual just to silence the coverage check.
unless: The guard path is explicitly classified as structural residual.
core.why: A guard path with no user/system flow route is a control path no user/system flow exercises, and one claimed by several routes has ambiguous ownership; exactly-one coverage keeps the user/system flow projection faithful to the flow router.
evidence: The projection-coverage check passes for every flow router subject at CONFIRM.
On failure, the finding identifies the flow router, the guard path, the route involved and a coverage status.
Every executable guard path maps to exactly one user/system flow route or is explicitly classified as structural residual.
verification: Enforced only at CONFIRM, the sole enforcement point; the finding is confirm-blocking; disposition strict, severity 4.

Scope: every flow router in the plan artifact, changed or unchanged; only executable guard paths are checked — non-executable flow router content is out of scope, and plan artifacts with no flow router subject are not checked.

The check is a projection-coverage check over the user/system flow projection: for each executable guard path not explicitly classified as structural residual, zero mapped user/system flow routes fails and two or more mapped routes fails; paths explicitly classified as structural residual are exempt from the exactly-one requirement.
A failure finding reports the flow router, the guard path, the route involved and a coverage status; the exact field names are realization details.
Observing the trigger needs new observers: the harness must supply the current plan phase, and the flow router validation subjects are identified by a subject observer, not by a file-kind fact.

fires: At CONFIRM, a flow router (new, edited or unchanged) has an executable guard path with no user/system flow route and no explicit structural-residual classification.
At CONFIRM, an executable guard path that is not explicitly classified as structural residual is mapped to two or more user/system flow routes.
At CONFIRM, after a user/system flow route was removed from the plan, an executable guard path it covered is left unmapped and not classified as structural residual.
doesNotFire: Any phase other than CONFIRM (e.g. while the planner is still drafting guards or routes); the check is enforced only at CONFIRM.
An executable guard path explicitly classified as structural residual.
Every executable guard path in the flow router maps to exactly one user/system flow route.
Plans that contain no flow router subject.
Non-executable content in a flow router (not a guard path).

neutralityNotes: This convention is already expressed entirely in plan-methodology terms (plan artifact, flow router, executable guard path, user/system flow route, structural residual, CONFIRM phase), so the core required no weakening or strengthening; the only realization-specific content in bun.json is identifiers of this one rule's validator and finding format (family/template/variant projection_covers_source::planner_user_system_flow_flow_router_guard_coverage, the failure-evidence field names, and the implementation/term ids held in the sidecar's audit), all classified bunOnly. profileRequirements is empty because bun.json references no path, suffix, artifact kind or idiom: the obligation lives entirely inside the plan artifact, and a realization resolves plan artifacts through the stack profile (e.g. roles.plan_artifact.kinds, roots.plan) without any per-rule profile need. The subject is not identified by a file-kind fact: the core keeps the Bun note's deference that flow router validation subjects require a new subject observer and that the harness must supply the phase (needs_new_observer). Severity 4 and disposition strict are kept in core:verification as per-rule facts, not profile keys.
